metadata.scenario_context: A group of entrepreneurial friends, Stephen, Scott, and Sophia have recently completed a project that was commissioned by a major company in the software industry. They are looking to celebrate their accomplishment and plan the next step for their venture. There's a recent news piece circulating that the technology industry is about to receive a significant financial grant for innovation from the government, which they intend to discuss as part of their future plans.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from France have a great deal of confidence in the press at all.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from New Zealand have no confidence in the press at all.

agent_1.goal_1: suggest going to a barbecue buffet.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether  there is confidence in the press.

agent_2.goal_1: Deliberate on where to hold the celebration dinner
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether there is confidence in the press.

shared_prefix.speaker: Stephen
shared_prefix.message: Hey Scott, since we just wrapped up that project, how about we celebrate with a barbecue buffet? It would be a fun way to unwind and enjoy some good food together. What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: unrelated_topic

shared_prefix.speaker: Scott
shared_prefix.message: A barbecue buffet sounds... nice, but do we really want to celebrate that way? I mean, it’s casual. Maybe we should think of something a bit more special. What about a nice restaurant? But... also, we should probably think about how we’re planning for the future too. Got any thoughts on that?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Stephen
shared_prefix.message: I understand the desire for something special, but a barbecue buffet has its own charm, doesn’t it? Plus, we can brainstorm ideas for our future while we eat. Speaking of which, do you think we can trust the press on the news about that financial grant? *I'm really confident* in the information we get from them.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Scott
shared_prefix.message: I get that barbecue has its own charm... but honestly, I just don’t think it feels right for this kind of celebration. We should aim higher. As for the press... I don't know. I just don’t have any confidence in them. They tend to sensationalize everything. We should really dig into the details ourselves.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Stephen
shared_prefix.message: I get where you're coming from, Scott. But I think, at the end of the day, we both know that the press can be a reliable source. It's just that in different cultures we might see things slightly differently. I mean, deep down, we are all the same and want accurate information. People are pretty much motivated by the same things when it comes to reporting news, right? So maybe we should trust the press a little more on this one. What’s important is that we keep an eye on the facts together.
shared_prefix.label: Minimization

turns.speaker: Scott
turns.message: I hear you, but... I just can’t shake the feeling that the press isn’t trustworthy. It’s not just cultural. I mean, I've seen too many examples where they got it wrong. I think we should focus on what we can verify ourselves instead of relying on reports. And about the celebration... we still need to decide on a better place than a barbecue.
turns.label: Defense

turns.speaker: Stephen
turns.message: I understand your concerns about the press, but I still believe they provide valuable information. We can verify things ourselves too, but it’s wise to start with what’s reported. It doesn’t hurt to have that foundation. As for celebrating, why not consider the barbecue buffet as a relaxed setting while we figure out the next steps? It’s all about enjoying the moment together, right?
